findings.fix: Remove `user-scalable=no` (and any `maximum-scale=1`) from the viewport meta tag so users can zoom.
findings.violation: `user-scalable=no` disables pinch-to-zoom, blocking low-vision users from magnifying content and violating WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text).

findings.evidence: Title is "Cascadia Regional Transit: Service Announcements" while the H1 reads "Fare and service announcements"
findings.fix: Align the `<title>` wording with the `<h1>`, e.g. "Cascadia Regional Transit: Fare and Service Announcements".
findings.violation: The page title and main heading describe the page differently (one omits "Fare", wording otherwise diverges), which is confusing for users and bookmarks/history entries.

findings.fix: Remove the inline color override or change it to a color that meets at least 4.5:1 contrast (e.g. #595959 or darker) against the page background.
findings.violation: #999999 on white gives a contrast ratio of roughly 2.85:1, failing WCAG AA's 4.5:1 minimum for normal text.

findings.evidence: Body text under this heading reads "Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk" and "Local residents may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app" with no mention of accessibility
findings.fix: Either rewrite the paragraphs to actually describe accessibility improvements, or retitle the section to match its real content.
findings.violation: The section heading promises accessibility-related content, but the paragraphs describe schedules and fare adjustments, not accessibility features - a content/heading mismatch that will mislead screen-reader users navigating by headings.

findings.evidence: Both paragraphs end with the identical sentence "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated sentence from one paragraph, keeping it only where it's contextually relevant.
findings.violation: Redundant repeated sentence across two adjacent paragraphs adds no information and reads as duplicated/boilerplate filler.

findings.evidence: `alt="A transit operator inspecting the platform screen doors before the morning shift."` under heading "Accessibility improvements"
findings.fix: Either use an image whose alt text illustrates an actual accessibility improvement, or rewrite the alt text to tie the image content to accessibility (e.g., noting an accessible boarding feature).
findings.violation: The image's alt text doesn't convey any accessibility-related information, so it doesn't support the section's stated topic for screen-reader users.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the mobile app. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Rewrite the second sentence to match the first action, e.g. remove it or replace with something like "Arrival times refresh automatically every minute."
findings.violation: Checking real-time arrivals is a read-only lookup, not a "request" that would generate a "confirmation message" - the two sentences describe inconsistent/mismatched actions.

findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` such as "Current zone status" inside the table.
findings.violation: The table has no `<caption>`, so screen-reader users navigating a list of tables get no description of what this table represents.

findings.evidence: "Passengers may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app." (compare to `s1-p2`: "Local residents may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app.")
findings.fix: Replace with content actually specific to weekend service, or remove the duplicate.
findings.violation: This near-duplicate sentence appears under "Weekend service," repeating content already given in the unrelated "Accessibility improvements" section, suggesting misplaced/copy-pasted content rather than weekend-specific information.

findings.fix: Replace the fixed pixel width with a responsive value, e.g. `max-width:960px; width:100%`.
findings.violation: A fixed 960px width will overflow the viewport on mobile screens (the page declares `width=device-width`), causing horizontal scrolling/clipping.

findings.evidence: `role="status"` combined with `style="height:60px;overflow:hidden"`, containing the sentence "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." (also duplicated from `s1-p1`)
findings.fix: Let the status card size to its content (remove fixed height/overflow:hidden, or use min-height) and write unique copy instead of reusing section 1's sentence.
findings.violation: A live status region with a fixed height and `overflow:hidden` will clip longer dynamically-inserted status updates, hiding information from all users including assistive-tech users who rely on the announced live region text matching what's visible; the duplicated sentence also repeats content already stated in section 1.

findings.fix: Darken the border color to at least 3:1 contrast against its background, e.g. #767676 or darker.
findings.violation: #9d9d9d on a typical white/light background is roughly 2.5:1 contrast, below the 3:1 minimum WCAG 1.4.11 requires for UI component boundaries that convey the control's shape.

findings.fix: Replace the div with a native `<button>` element and clarify what it deletes (or remove it if it's leftover from another component).
findings.violation: This is a custom interactive control built from a `<div>` instead of a native `<button>`; the markup alone gives no evidence of keyboard activation handling (Enter/Space), which native buttons provide for free, and its purpose ("Delete item") is unclear/out of place on a service-announcements page with no visible "item" to delete.

findings.evidence: Steps "Choose a plan", "Enter payment details", "Confirm your order"
findings.fix: Remove this wizard if it doesn't belong on the page, or if intentional, mark the active step with `aria-current="step"` and give the content transit-relevant copy.
findings.violation: This checkout-style wizard content is unrelated to weekend transit service announcements, and none of the step `<div>`s indicate which step is current (no `aria-current` or similar), leaving both sighted and assistive-tech users unable to tell progress.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list` inside a sentence about "upcoming adjustments," in the "Weekend service" section
findings.fix: Change the link text to describe the actual target, e.g. "read the fare adjustment history."
findings.violation: The link text says "accessibility improvements list" but points to `/fares/history` and sits in a paragraph about fare/schedule adjustments - the link text doesn't describe its actual destination, misleading users (especially screen-reader users who scan link text out of context).

findings.fix: Change the label's `for` to `topic` (or change the select's id to `topic-alt`) so they match.
findings.violation: The label's `for` attribute references `topic-alt`, which doesn't exist, while the select's actual id is `topic` - the label is not programmatically associated with the control, so screen readers and click-to-focus won't connect them.

findings.evidence: Label text "Phone number (required)" but `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">` has no `required` or `aria-required` attribute
findings.violation: The visible label claims the field is required, but nothing in the markup enforces or exposes that to assistive technology, so screen-reader users won't know it's mandatory and validation won't trigger.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">` present in the static markup with no prior user input
findings.fix: Set `aria-invalid="false"` (or omit it) by default and only set it to `"true"` dynamically after a failed validation attempt.
findings.violation: Marking the field invalid before the user has interacted with it falsely signals an error on page load for both sighted users and assistive-tech users.

findings.evidence: `Enter a 6 character code...`
findings.violation: The error message is not linked to the promo input via `aria-describedby`, so screen-reader users focused on the field won't hear the error text associated with it.
